patient.name: Renata Solis
patient.chiefComplaint: 38 weeks pregnant, sudden gush of fluid followed by feeling something in the vagina

history.hpi: G2P1 at 38 weeks gestation. Patient reports her water broke approximately 10 minutes ago with a large gush of clear fluid, immediately followed by a sensation of something protruding from the vagina and an urge to push. She is now on hands and knees per her husband's instruction after he saw a loop of umbilical cord at the vaginal opening. Contractions are strong and about 3 minutes apart.
pastMedical: Uncomplicated first pregnancy/vaginal delivery 3 years ago
history.events: Membranes ruptured spontaneously at home; husband saw the cord and called 911 immediately, placed patient in knee-chest position on instruction from the dispatcher

scene.dispatch: 30-year-old female, pregnant, water broke, patient reports something protruding, residence
scene.location: Single-family home, master bedroom, patient positioned on hands and knees on the bed per dispatcher pre-arrival instructions
scene.safety: No hazards to crew noted; adequate lighting available in bedroom
scene.bystanders: Husband present, followed dispatcher's pre-arrival instructions to place patient in knee-chest position
visualCues: Patient in knee-chest position on the bed, visibly anxious
Loop of pulsating umbilical cord visible at the vaginal opening
Clear amniotic fluid soaking the sheets
Strong contractions visibly gripping the patient every few minutes
Husband kneeling beside the bed holding patient's hand

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 30-year-old G2P1 female at 38 weeks in the knee-chest position with a visible, pulsating loop of umbilical cord protruding from the vaginal opening. Strong contractions are ongoing.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Patent, speaking in full sentences between contractions
otherFindings: Pulsating loop of umbilical cord visible at introitus
No fetal head or presenting part visible yet
Patient maintaining knee-chest position with assistance
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Something's coming out of me, please help, is my baby okay?"

transitions.if: Cord manually elevated off presenting part
transitions.condition: Crew immediately recognizes the prolapsed cord as an obstetric emergency and places a gloved hand into the vagina to gently lift the presenting part off the cord to relieve compression.
Crew focuses on packaging for transport or other assessment before performing manual elevation of the presenting part off the cord.

phases.name: Cord manually elevated off presenting part
phases.description: Crew places a gloved hand into the vagina and gently lifts the fetal presenting part off the cord to relieve compression, assesses for cord pulsations, and wraps the exposed cord in moist sterile gauze.
phases.triggerCondition: Recognizing the classic presentation of prolapsed cord (visible pulsating cord at the introitus with ruptured membranes), the crew immediately performs manual elevation to relieve cord compression before any further assessment or packaging.

otherFindings: Cord pulsations palpable and strong once compression relieved
Prolapsed cord wrapped in moist sterile gauze
Presenting part held off the cord with sustained manual pressure
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Okay, okay, I can feel your hand, just tell me what to do."

expectedActions.shortAction: Place gloved hand into vagina; gently lift presenting part off the prolapsed cord
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Prolapsed Umbilical Cord: Place gloved hand into vagina and gently lift head/body off the cord
expectedActions.rationale: Relieves compression of the cord between the fetal presenting part and the maternal pelvis, restoring fetal blood flow.

expectedActions.shortAction: Assess cord for pulsations after relieving compression
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Assess for pulsations in cord, if no pulses are felt, lift the presenting part off the cord
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms whether manual elevation has restored fetal circulation through the cord.

expectedActions.shortAction: Wrap the prolapsed cord in moist sterile gauze
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Wrap the prolapsed cord in moist sterile gauze
expectedActions.rationale: Prevents desiccation and further trauma to the exposed cord during transport.

transitions.condition: With the cord decompressed and pulsating well, the crew optimizes maternal positioning and initiates immediate transport while maintaining manual elevation throughout.

phases.name: Position optimized, rapid transport initiated
phases.description: Crew maintains sustained manual elevation of the presenting part off the cord, positions the mother in extreme Trendelenburg or knee-chest with hips elevated, applies high-flow oxygen, and expedites transport with advance notification to the receiving facility.
phases.triggerCondition: With cord pulsations confirmed and the presenting part held off the cord, the crew optimizes positioning to further relieve compression and moves immediately to transport given the time-critical nature of the emergency.

otherFindings: Extreme Trendelenburg with hips elevated maintained during transport
Manual elevation of presenting part sustained continuously
Receiving facility notified and OB team prepared for emergent cesarean
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Please don't stop, please don't let go."

expectedActions.shortAction: Place mother in prone knee-chest or extreme Trendelenburg with hips elevated
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If previous techniques are not successful, mother should be placed in prone knee-chest position or extreme Trendelenburg with hips elevated
expectedActions.rationale: Uses gravity to further shift the presenting part away from the cord and reduce compression.

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply high-flow oxygen to mother; expedite transport to appropriate receiving facility
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If complications of delivery occur, apply high flow oxygen to mother and expedite transport to the appropriate receiving facility. Maternal resuscitation is critical for best fetal outcome
expectedActions.rationale: Maximizes fetal oxygen delivery and gets the patient to definitive care (likely emergent cesarean) as quickly as possible.

expectedActions.shortAction: Contact medical direction/receiving facility to prepare team for prolapsed cord
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Notify medical direction/receiving facility if: Prolapsed umbilical cord
expectedActions.rationale: Allows the receiving OB team to prepare for immediate emergent delivery on arrival.

phases.name: Manual elevation delayed
phases.description: Crew delays manual elevation of the presenting part off the cord in favor of packaging or other assessment, allowing sustained cord compression during ongoing strong contractions.
phases.triggerCondition: The crew becomes focused on positioning for transport or other assessment steps before addressing the cord compression directly, leaving the presenting part to continue compressing the cord during contractions.

otherFindings: Cord pulsations noticeably weaker on repeat check
Contraction just occurred with visible cord compression
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Why aren't you doing anything, is my baby moving?"

expectedActions.shortAction: Immediately place gloved hand into vagina to lift presenting part off cord
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Prolapsed Umbilical Cord: Place gloved hand into vagina and gently lift head/body off the cord. Assess for pulsations in cord, if no pulses are felt, lift the presenting part off the cord
expectedActions.rationale: Weakening cord pulsations indicate worsening fetal compromise from ongoing compression; manual elevation must be performed without further delay.
